### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A45 handed over to one of the three alternatives A19, A20 or A25 (about 85 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, split roughly 31/26/28), and A26 followed two event steps later in about 84 in 100 observations; in the later window, A45 leads almost directly to A26 (about 89 in 100, one event step away). [DIR006, LAG008]
- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 each led almost exclusively to A26 (about 89–98 in 100 of their outgoing transitions); in the later window they lead instead to A28 (about 38–51 in 100) and A32 (about 43–58 in 100), with A20→A28 now a one-step adjacency (about 97 in 100 of 36 observations), while the direct A25→A26 step, seen in 63 traces earlier, is nearly unobserved (1 observation). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG003]
- In the earlier window, A27 led to A28 (about 98 in 100) and A28 to A32 (about 94 in 100), each in one step; in the later window each sends about half of its transitions to the alternative group (about 48 and 51 in 100), so A27→A28 and A28→A32 now split roughly 50/50 between one and two steps, and A27 reaches A32 in three steps instead of two. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG006]
- Precedence flipped: earlier, A19, A20 and A25 each ran before A26 and before A27 in about 30–38 in 100 traces and virtually never after; later, A26 and A27 each run before them in about 30–36 in 100 and never the reverse. Around A28 the later window shows both orders (about 15–22 in 100 each way) where earlier the group always came first (about 32–37 in 100). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- Event positions shifted accordingly: the mean position of A19, A20 and A25 moved from about 0.31–0.34 to about 0.58–0.59 of the trace, while A26 and A27 moved slightly earlier (about 0.35→0.32 and 0.58→0.55). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Participation stayed similar: A19 appears in about 38 vs 30 in 100 traces, A20 about 32 vs 34, A25 about 32 vs 38; A26 and A27 occur in all traces in both windows, A28 and A45 in essentially all. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the group of alternative activities A19, A20 and A25 — roughly one of which still executes per case — was relocated from before A26 to the late segment of the flow. In the earlier window the order ran A45 → (A19 | A20 | A25) → A26 → A27 → A28 → A32; in the later window it runs A45 → A26 → A27, and the group then executes after A27 and before A32, before A28 in about half of the cases and after A28 in the other half, reaching A32 directly or via A28. This rests on direct relational evidence: reversed precedence with A26 and A27, mixed order around A28, new and vanished one-step adjacencies exactly at the old and new block boundaries, matching successor changes at A45, A27 and A28, and consistent position shifts. Stable participation rules out the alternatives having been added, removed or made optional. The volume of flagged items (27 against about 0.63 expected without a change) is far beyond what random re-splits of these windows produce, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 in 1000 random re-splits. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG003, LAG006, LAG008, REL001, REL003, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, screening]

Limitations: the later-window sequence is reconstructed from pairwise relations and event positions, so the evidence cannot establish whether the group's new placement is one fixed position or varies case by case around A28; it can only show that the group now always follows A27 and precedes A32. For the new adjacencies, the earlier window contains only 1 observation (A20→A28, A20→A32, A28→A20), so the earlier absence of those pairs rests mainly on the successor and precedence items. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is case-dependent routing that places the group differently in different traces rather than a single new position. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG006, DIR004, DIR005, REL002, REL005, REL007]

Other differences: the take-up of the individual alternatives shifted modestly (A19 about 38→31 in 100 traces, A25 about 32→38 in 100); with 200 traces per window the evidence cannot establish whether these shifts exceed sampling variation, and they are not part of the main hypothesis. [POS001, POS002, POS003]
